title: Install
text:
quarto add tiagojct/pequod-quarto
This drops the extension under _extensions/tiagojct/pequod/ and _extensions/tiagojct/pequod-dark/. Quarto’s resolver honours the org-prefixed install path automatically.

title: Install
text:
Known issues






Warning



Single-file render under org-prefixed install. Quarto’s resolver has a known bug where quarto render subdir/chapter.qmd --to pequod-html may fail to find the extension when installed at _extensions/<org>/<name>/. Workarounds: render project-wide (quarto render), or flatten the extension path to _extensions/<name>/ for that project.








Warning



Typst PDF requires the bundled TTFs. The extension ships static-weight Atkinson Hyperlegible Next + Mono TTFs under _extensions/pequod/fonts/. If you remove that directory, Typst falls back to its built-in defaults (Libertinus Serif + DejaVu Sans Mono) and the visual identity collapses.








Warning



pequod-html dark mode requires theme-toggle: true. Set it in your project’s _quarto.yml to surface the navbar control that flips between the light and dark stylesheets:
format:
  pequod-html:
    theme-toggle: true

title: Formats
text: The extension contributes four Quarto formats. Each one is selected by name in the format: key of a .qmd frontmatter or a project _quarto.yml. All four formats share the same palette tokens, font stacks, and syntax-highlighting mapping — switching formats does not mean re-learning the visual language.

title: Formats
text:
pequod-revealjs — slide decks (light)
---
title: "Your title"
format: pequod-revealjs
---
Defaults that ship: 1600 × 900 surface, center: true (slides vertically centred by reveal), slide-number: c/t, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next body, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono code. Per-slide opt-outs:
## A photo wall {.no-footer .no-logo}
The deck title slide and H1 section dividers already have the footer and logo hidden by convention.

title: Formats
text:
pequod-dark-revealjs — slide decks (dark)
format: pequod-dark-revealjs
Same shape as the light variant, deep-ink ground, paper-tone text, dark crew accents.

title: Formats
text:
pequod-html — documents (light + dark)
format:
  pequod-html:
    theme-toggle: true   # surfaces the navbar light/dark control
What’s wired by default:

theme: { light: pequod-html.scss, dark: pequod-html-dark.scss }
highlight-style: { light: pequod.theme, dark: pequod-dark.theme }
code-copy: true, code-overflow: wrap
smooth-scroll: true, anchor-sections: true
link-external-newwindow: true (external links open new tab)
fig-cap-location: bottom, tbl-cap-location: top

Print stylesheet built in: hides navbar / sidebar / TOC / footer, prints (href) after external links, strips surface fills, prevents page breaks inside headings / figures / tables.

title: Formats
text:
pequod-typst — PDF output
format: pequod-typst
What’s wired by default:

A4 paper, 2.5 cm margins
mainfont: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", monofont: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono", codefont: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono" (Quarto’s Typst template reads codefont, not monofont, for show raw)
font-paths: [fonts] relative to the extension dir so the bundled static-weight TTFs load under the org-prefixed install
pequod-typst.typ include that overrides Quarto’s default #callout(...) to remap Bootstrap colours to the crew

title: Customise
Customise
Customise
text:
Replace the body / mono fonts
The font stacks are themselves !default tokens. Override in my-overrides.scss:
$font-family-sans-serif: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif !default;
$font-family-monospace:  "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace !default;
If you replace the body font, you almost certainly also want to swap the mainfont: / monofont: YAML keys so reveal and Typst pick the same family up:
format:
  pequod-revealjs:
    theme:
      - my-overrides.scss
    mainfont: "IBM Plex Sans"
    monofont: "JetBrains Mono"
Self-hosted woff2 fonts can be wired with Quarto’s standard @font-face recipe in your own include-in-header partial.

title: Customise
text:
Recolour the data-viz palette
Eight categorical chart slots live in _pequod-palette.scss as $pequod-chart-1..8-light / …-dark. Override individual slots:
// my-overrides.scss
$pequod-chart-1-light: #2A2A2A !default;   // softer black for the
                                           // primary series
The active set is exported as --pequod-chart-1..8 CSS custom properties on :root so Observable / htmlwidgets / plain JS can pick them up at runtime. See Data viz for usage.

title: Customise
text:
Add a logo (once, used everywhere)
The bundled pequod.lua filter forwards a single pequod.logo metadata key to the format-specific keys that Quarto / Reveal consume. Set in your project _quarto.yml:
pequod:
  logo: assets/logo.svg
The filter writes to meta.logo (reveal), meta.website.navbar.logo (websites) and meta.book.navbar.logo (books), but only if the user has not already set them.

title: Customise
section: Add an Open Graph card image
text:
Add an Open Graph card image
Same filter, same key shape:
pequod:
  og-image: assets/og-card.png
The filter resolves og:image in this order: pequod.og-image → website.open-graph.image → per-page og-image. Twitter Card upgrades to summary_large_image when an image is set.

title: Customise
text:
Per-slide opt-outs (reveal)
Quarto markdown’s curly attribute syntax carries through:
## A photo wall {.no-footer .no-logo}
The deck title slide and H1 section dividers already hide the footer and logo by convention. .no-footer / .no-logo only need to be added on body slides where the corner mark would clash with the content.

title: Customise
text:
Highlight pill
Spans marked with .highlight or <mark> get a warm-paper-deep background in light mode and a deep-paper-light background in dark mode. Both $highlight-bg and $highlight-color are !default tokens; override per-mode in your pequod.scss / pequod-dark.scss overrides file.

title: Accessibility
text: The theme treats accessibility as a non-negotiable requirement, not a nice-to-have. Every accent surface, every link, every callout, every focus cue has been audited against WCAG 2.2 AA at minimum.

title: Accessibility
text:
Two-channel link cue
Prose links carry three distinguishing cues, not one:

Colour — Starbuck blue (light) / Starbuck light (dark)
Underline — 2 px Starbuck-tinted, 0.18em underline offset
Weight — 500 (medium) rather than the body’s 400

The combination of colour-plus-underline satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (do not rely on colour alone). On monochrome renderers (e-paper, fax printouts, high-contrast OS modes), the underline and weight cues still distinguish links from body text.
The cue is scoped to main, article, .content, and .quarto-document-content so navbar / sidebar / TOC / footer / anchor / citation links keep their own treatments and don’t drown the page in underlines.

The colour-coded left rule is reinforced by a tinted header with the same crew colour and a Bootstrap icon — so the callout type is distinguishable to colour-blind readers (the rule + icon + label text carry the information together).

title: Accessibility
text:
Reduced motion
Both formats honour prefers-reduced-motion: reduce:

HTML disables theme smooth-scroll. Bootstrap 5’s own $enable-reduced-motion: true covers component-level animations (modals, dropdowns, …).
Reveal clamps animation-duration and transition-duration to 0.01ms on every .reveal * descendant. Reveal’s slide transition is already set to none by default in the extension, but downstream callouts and fragment animations can still animate without this clamp.

title: Accessibility
text:
Print
The HTML format ships a print stylesheet that:

Hides navbar / sidebar / TOC / footer / repo actions / search
Prints (href) after every external link so readers on paper can follow them
Strips code-block surface fills (saves toner)
Prevents page breaks inside headings, figures, and tables

External link URLs are excluded for localhost, citations, and the .no-underline class.

title: Accessibility
text:
Skip nav
Quarto’s built-in skip-link sits at the top of every HTML page (<a class="skip-link" href="#quarto-content">Skip to content</a>). The theme styles the focused state with the same body-colour outline + Starbuck glow as the rest of the focus indicators.

title: Accessibility
text:
Self-hosted fonts (GDPR + offline)
Both Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono are shipped as base64-inlined woff2 inside _pequod-fonts.scss. No network requests fire at page-load time; the page renders the institutional typography even with the user offline or with a strict Content-Security-Policy font-src 'self' rule.
The Typst format ships static-weight TTFs under _extensions/pequod/fonts/ for the same reason — Typst loads them through font-paths: [fonts] (relative to the extension dir).

title: Data viz
text:
Restraint
The eight slots are deliberate. Six of them carry strong crew identity; the seventh (Pip) is a warm dark yellow that doesn’t read well as a primary series colour on the dark variant; the eighth (Daggoo) is a deep brown. Don’t paint every series — most charts only need two or three slots. The point of a constrained palette is that the first colour a reader sees is always institutional.

title: Pequod for Quarto
text: A Quarto extension that applies the Pequod palette to slide decks, documents, and PDFs. Body and headings render in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next; code renders in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono. Both fonts are bundled inside the theme — no Google Fonts CDN at render time, GDPR-clean, offline-renderable, cached once per site.

title: Pequod for Quarto
text:
Quick look






Note



This very documentation site is rendered with pequod-html. The theme-toggle in the navbar flips between the warm-paper and deep-ink variants — the toggle ships with the extension and works out of the box once theme-toggle: true is set in your project’s _quarto.yml.


# Inline code, code blocks, and tables all read the same register.
import numpy as np

def loss(theta: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mean squared error for a linear model."""
    return float(np.mean((x @ theta - y) ** 2))

A whale-ship was my Yale College and my Harvard.
